title: Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana: Rs 1.20 Lakh for Girl Child
meta_description: Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana provides Rs 1.20 lakh total to girl children through education milestones. Eligibility, application, and milestone payment details.

hero.one_liner: Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana deposits Rs 61,000 for a girl child in stages from birth to graduation, growing to about Rs 1.20 lakh with interest. Live since April 2026.

what_is_it: Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is the Delhi government's flagship girl child welfare scheme, designed to provide a cumulative financial benefit of Rs 1.20 lakh (Rs 1,20,000) to each eligible girl child through a carefully structured series of milestone-linked payouts tied to her education and key life stages. The scheme aims to directly address the economic vulnerability that often surrounds the birth of a girl child in low-income Delhi households and to strongly incentivise parents to keep their daughters in school through higher education, creating a lasting financial stake in each daughter's educational journey.

The name 'Lakhpati Bitiya' literally means 'daughter worth a lakh' and reflects the scheme's intent to demonstrate through a sustained financial commitment that a girl child is as valued as a boy child in the eyes of the state. The cumulative Rs 1.20 lakh benefit is structured across multiple disbursements, ensuring that the family receives meaningful support at critical junctures in the girl's upbringing and education rather than as a single one-time payment.

eligibility_filters.notes: Girl child born in Delhi, family resident 3+ years, annual income up to Rs 1.20 lakh, max two girls. Rs 61,000 deposited in milestone stages via SBI Life, maturing to about Rs 1.20 lakh with interest. Live since 1 April 2026, replacing the old Ladli Scheme. Apply on the Delhi e-District portal. Must stay unmarried till 18.

how_to_apply.title: Register the birth
how_to_apply.description: Complete the girl child's birth registration at the nearest MCD (municipal corporation) office or through the online birth registration portal within the stipulated time. A valid birth certificate is the foundational document required for the scheme; delayed registration may result in loss of the first milestone payout.

how_to_apply.title: Apply at anganwadi or WCD office
how_to_apply.description: Visit the nearest anganwadi centre, Mahila Shakti Kendra, or district WCD office with the birth certificate, mother's Aadhaar card, Delhi domicile proof (voter ID), and income certificate. Staff will assist with filling the registration form and submit it to the department for verification.

how_to_apply.title: Or apply online via e-District Delhi
how_to_apply.description: Go to edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in, create an account or log in, and navigate to the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana application form. Upload scanned copies of the required documents (birth certificate, Aadhaar, domicile proof, income certificate, bank account details) and submit the application online.

how_to_apply.title: Receive birth milestone payment
how_to_apply.description: After verification of the birth registration application, the first milestone payout is credited to the mother's Aadhaar-linked bank account via DBT. Keep the acknowledgement receipt and bank credit confirmation for your records.

how_to_apply.title: Submit school milestone proofs
how_to_apply.description: At each subsequent education milestone (Class 1 admission, Class 6, 9, 11 entry, and higher education enrollment), submit the girl's school enrollment certificate or admission letter to the WCD department or through the e-District portal to trigger the next milestone payout.

how_to_apply.title: Track and receive payouts
how_to_apply.description: Each verified milestone triggers a DBT credit to the mother's Aadhaar-linked bank account. Log in to edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in or visit the WCD office to track your application's payout history and confirm that all milestone amounts have been received correctly.

ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Govt of Delhi

extra_sections.heading: What Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana Is
content: The scheme is targeted at girl children born in Delhi to families that meet the income and domicile criteria, with registration completed after birth to begin receiving payouts at birth registration and subsequent school enrollment stages. The girl child's mother or female guardian is the primary account holder, with each milestone amount transferred directly via DBT to her Aadhaar-linked bank account upon milestone verification.

Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is positioned as a successor or complement to the older Delhi Ladli Scheme, which was one of India's first state-level girl child financial incentive schemes, launched in 2008. While the Ladli Scheme focuses on a different benefit structure and payout timeline, the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana represents an enhanced and higher-value commitment by the Delhi government to the welfare of girl children from economically weaker sections.

extra_sections.heading: What Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana Is More
content: The scheme's milestone-based structure is deliberately designed to create sustained engagement between the family and the education system. By releasing funds at school admission, grade transitions, and higher education enrollment, the scheme creates a financial incentive at each point where dropout rates are known to rise, particularly at the Class 6, 9, and 11 transitions when families in low-income households often pull girls out of school.

Eligibility for the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is primarily based on Delhi domicile and family income, with the girl child needing to be born in Delhi or registered as a Delhi resident and the family falling within the EWS or lower-income category as defined in the official notification. The exact income ceiling may be revised annually, so families should check the current year's official guidelines at the WCD department or on the Delhi government website before applying.

extra_sections.title: How the Rs 1.20 Lakh Actually Works
extra_sections.content:
The Delhi government deposits Rs 61,000 in staged installments through SBI Life, from birth to graduation. With interest over the years, this grows to about Rs 1.20 to 1.25 lakh by the time the girl finishes her studies.

So Rs 61,000 is what the state puts in, and Rs 1.20 lakh is roughly what the girl gets at maturity. The scheme is live from 1 April 2026, replacing the old Ladli Scheme.

extra_sections.heading: The Milestone Payment Structure
content: The birth of the girl child must be registered under the Civil Registration System (birth registration) within a specified period of the birth date for the family to become eligible for the earliest payout. Delayed birth registration can result in loss of the first milestone benefit, so families are encouraged to complete birth registration promptly at the local municipal corporation office or through the online birth registration portal.

The scheme is administered by the Women and Child Development (WCD) Department of the Delhi government, working in coordination with the Education Department for school milestone verifications and the urban local body (MCD) for birth registration tracking. Applications are submitted through the Delhi government welfare portal or at the nearest district WCD office or anganwadi centre.

extra_sections.heading: The Milestone Payment Structure More
content: Under the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana, each education milestone is verified through school records before the corresponding payout is released; the school must confirm to the WCD department that the girl is enrolled and attending the relevant class, after which the next DBT tranche is initiated. This verification step ensures the benefit remains continuously tied to actual educational participation rather than being paid regardless of dropout.

The scheme covers girl children from birth through graduation or professional course completion, with each stage from birth to Class 1, Class 6, Class 9, Class 11, and higher education enrollment representing a milestone payout. The higher amounts are reserved for the later education stages to maximise the financial incentive for families to keep their daughters in school through higher secondary and tertiary education.

extra_sections.heading: The Stage-Wise Deposits
content: For families with more than one girl child, each daughter is registered separately and entitled to the full Rs 1.20 lakh benefit independently. This means a family with two daughters would cumulatively receive Rs 2.40 lakh over the years if both daughters complete the educational milestones, creating a meaningful long-term financial asset for the household.

The funds accumulated under the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana are intended to contribute to the girl's higher education or vocational training costs, reduce the financial burden on families at the time of the girl's marriage, and generally strengthen the household's financial position by channelling public resources specifically to daughters. The scheme's structure ensures the money is not extracted prematurely but builds over the girl's school years.

Documents required for registration under the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana include the girl child's birth certificate, the mother or guardian's Aadhaar card, proof of Delhi domicile (Delhi voter ID or domicile certificate of the parent), income certificate from a competent authority, and an Aadhaar-linked bank account in the mother's or guardian's name. For subsequent milestone payouts, the girl's school enrollment certificate or progress report must be submitted.

The Delhi government has made digital enrollment possible through the e-District Delhi portal (edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in), where parents can register their daughter for the scheme, upload documents, and track payout status. Physical applications can also be submitted at Mahila Shakti Kendras, district WCD offices, or through the anganwadi network for families without internet access.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: Awareness about the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is spread through the anganwadi network, which reaches households in Delhi's lower-income areas where new mothers are already connected to the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS). ASHA workers and anganwadi workers are trained to inform eligible families about the registration process and to assist with initial documentation at the anganwadi centre.

The long-term social objective of the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is to shift attitudes toward the girl child among low-income families by making the birth of a daughter financially positive rather than financially burdensome. In communities where son preference persists due to economic reasons, schemes like Lakhpati Bitiya directly counteract the financial calculus that disadvantages girls by making the state a financial partner in the girl's upbringing.

Families who move out of Delhi after enrolling in the scheme may face complications with subsequent milestone payouts, as the scheme is specific to Delhi residents. Beneficiaries should inform the WCD department if they relocate permanently, and in such cases the continued eligibility for future milestone payouts would depend on the specific rules in the current official notification.

The payout amounts at each milestone are proportioned to ensure that families receive a meaningful sum at each stage while retaining most of the value for the later, more education-critical transitions. Early-stage payouts (birth, Class 1 entry) are smaller, while the payouts at Class 9 entry, Class 11 entry, and higher education enrollment are larger, reflecting the higher cost and higher dropout risk associated with those transitions.

extra_sections.title: Replaced the 2008 Ladli Scheme
extra_sections.desc:
The old Delhi Ladli Scheme closed on 31 March 2026, and Lakhpati Bitiya started from 1 April 2026 with higher benefits.

Existing Ladli beneficiaries continue to get their pending entitlements, and their data is moving to the new portal. New girls register only under Lakhpati Bitiya.

extra_sections.heading: Lakhpati Bitiya vs the Old Ladli Scheme
content: Parents and guardians registering their daughters under the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana should maintain careful records of all milestone verifications and DBT credit receipts, as these may be needed for future milestone releases. Keeping a file with the registration acknowledgement, each school certificate submitted, and the corresponding bank credit SMS or passbook entry provides a complete record that can be referenced if any dispute or delay arises in subsequent payouts.

The Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana works best when integrated with the girl's school enrollment under the Right to Education (RTE) Act and Delhi government school admission processes. Families who enroll their daughters in Delhi government schools as part of the RTE mandate can simultaneously complete the Lakhpati Bitiya milestone submission for the Class 1 payout, streamlining the administrative process and reducing the number of separate visits to government offices.

extra_sections.heading: Lakhpati Bitiya vs the Old Ladli Scheme More
content: Girl children who are orphaned or living with grandparents or other extended family members can also be registered under the scheme with the female guardian as the account holder for payouts. The Delhi WCD department has specific provisions for such cases, and the anganwadi worker in the girl's area can provide guidance on the documentation needed for non-parental guardian registrations.

The impact of the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana extends beyond direct cash transfers: by requiring school enrollment certificates at each milestone, the scheme also functions as an indirect attendance monitoring tool that creates a built-in financial incentive for parents to keep daughters enrolled throughout the school years. Research on similar girl child milestone schemes in other states has found measurable improvements in school retention rates in communities with high scheme penetration.

extra_sections.title: Apply Within the Time Window
extra_sections.content:
Register within one year of birth, or within 90 days of admission at each stage like Class 1, 6, 9, and 11. Late applications may be accepted at later stages, but you only get benefits from that stage onward.

Missing the birth registration window does not fully disqualify you, but you lose the earlier deposits.

extra_sections.heading: How to Register
content: The coordination between the WCD department and the Delhi government's Education Department is essential for the smooth functioning of the milestone verification process. School principals and teachers are informed about the scheme and are expected to issue enrollment certificates promptly when parents or guardians request them for Lakhpati Bitiya milestone submissions, treating these as priority documents.

For girl children born in government hospitals or delivered by institutional delivery facilitated by the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), the birth certificate is typically generated by the hospital and the registration details are fed into the Civil Registration System directly, making the documentation process for the Lakhpati Bitiya birth milestone simpler. Parents only need to collect the official birth certificate from the municipal corporation and submit it to the WCD office.

extra_sections.heading: How to Register More
content: Delhi's urban demography includes a large number of women who migrated from other states and whose daughters are born in Delhi; these girls are full Delhi residents from birth and are eligible for the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana if the family meets the income criteria, regardless of the parents' state of origin. The domicile requirement applies to the girl child's registration and residence, not to where the parents originally came from.

The scheme's integration with the anganwadi network also means that anganwadi workers can track which registered girl children in their catchment area have upcoming milestones (such as turning school-age for Class 1 entry) and proactively remind families to submit the required documents. This proactive outreach is important for reducing the number of families who miss a milestone payout simply due to lack of awareness.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and Deadlines
content: The Delhi government periodically reviews the milestone payout amounts under the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana and may revise them upward to account for inflation and increased education costs. Beneficiaries who registered their daughters in an earlier year should check the WCD department website for any updates to the payout schedule when submitting documents for subsequent milestones, as the amounts for later stages may have changed since initial registration.

Beyond the individual family benefits, the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana contributes to Delhi's commitment to gender equity in education outcomes. Delhi already has relatively higher female literacy and school attendance rates compared to many other Indian states, and schemes like Lakhpati Bitiya reinforce this by addressing the financial barriers that disproportionately affect girls' continued education at the secondary and higher secondary levels where dropout rates are highest.

extra_sections.title: Documents and Deadlines Notes
extra_sections.content:
Girls who successfully complete all milestones of the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana and receive the full Rs 1.20 lakh will have accumulated a meaningful financial asset by the time they enter higher education. This amount, when used for college fees, vocational training, or as seed capital for a small business, can represent a transformative resource for a young woman from an economically disadvantaged background in Delhi.

The scheme also reduces the pressure on families to arrange dowry by demonstrating that the state values the girl child's education and development, not just her marriage. While dowry is illegal in India, informal expectations remain in many communities; the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana's framing of the girl child as an economic asset through state investment directly challenges this narrative by placing the highest financial payout at the higher education stage rather than the marriage stage.

extra_sections.heading: The Unmarried-Till-18 Condition
content: For the Delhi WCD department, the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana's data on milestone completions also provides valuable insight into where girls are dropping out of the education system. If a large number of registered girls fail to claim the Class 9 or Class 11 milestone payouts, it signals elevated dropout risk at those transitions and can help the department target remedial interventions like scholarship support, counselling, or bridge courses to retain girls in school.

Families who have already registered under the older Delhi Ladli Scheme should check with the WCD department whether the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is available as an additional and separate entitlement or whether it replaces the Ladli Scheme for new registrations going forward. The official notification for the current academic year will clarify the precise relationship between the two schemes and whether a girl child already enrolled in Ladli can also be separately registered in the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana.

faqs.question: What is Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is the Delhi government's girl child welfare scheme that provides a total of Rs 1.20 lakh (Rs 1,20,000) per girl child through milestone-linked DBT payouts at birth, Class 1 entry, Class 6, 9, 11, and higher education enrollment. It targets EWS and low-income families with Delhi domicile.

faqs.question: How much money is given under Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Rs 1.20 lakh (Rs 1,20,000) in total per girl child, distributed across multiple milestone-linked payouts. The amounts at each milestone vary, with higher amounts reserved for later education stages like Class 11 and higher education enrollment.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Girl children born to EWS or low-income families who are Delhi residents (as evidenced by Delhi voter ID or domicile certificate of the parent). The income ceiling and other eligibility conditions are defined in the official notification and should be verified at the time of application.

faqs.question: What are the milestones for payment under Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Payments are made at birth registration, Class 1 school admission, Class 6 admission, Class 9 admission, Class 11 admission, and higher education enrollment. Each milestone triggers a separate DBT payout to the mother's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Apply online at edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in or visit the nearest anganwadi centre, Mahila Shakti Kendra, or district WCD office. You need the girl's birth certificate, mother's Aadhaar card, Delhi domicile proof, income certificate, and an Aadhaar-linked bank account in the mother's name.

faqs.question: Is Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana the same as Delhi Ladli Scheme?
faqs.answer:
No, they are separate schemes. The Delhi Ladli Scheme (launched 2008) provides milestone-based amounts maturing into a bond after age 18.

The Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana is a higher-value scheme providing Rs 1.20 lakh total through direct DBT payouts. A girl child may be eligible for one or both depending on the official notifications.

faqs.question: If I have two daughters, do both get Rs 1.20 lakh?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Each eligible girl child is registered separately and entitled to the full Rs 1.20 lakh benefit independently.

A family with two daughters would receive Rs 2.40 lakh total if both daughters complete all milestones.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana?
faqs.answer: Girl child's birth certificate, mother or guardian's Aadhaar card, Delhi domicile proof (voter ID or domicile certificate), income certificate from a competent authority, and an Aadhaar-linked bank account in the mother's or guardian's name. For subsequent milestone payouts, school enrollment certificates are also needed.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss registering at birth?
faqs.answer:
Late registration may result in loss of the birth-stage payout. However, the family may still be eligible for subsequent milestone payouts if the girl is registered under the scheme before the next milestone (Class 1 entry).

Contact the nearest WCD office for guidance on late registrations.

faqs.question: Is the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana available for girls studying outside Delhi?
faqs.answer:
The scheme is based on Delhi domicile of the family, not the location of the school. However, school milestone verifications typically require documentation from the enrolled school.

Families whose daughters study outside Delhi should check with the WCD department whether out-of-Delhi school certificates are accepted for milestone releases.
